claims.statement: For every nonempty ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star profile, with N=sum_i r_i, h=1+2a_2+4a_3+7a_4, C=G product_i B_(r_i), E=zL^N, U_i=G B_(r_i-1) product_(u!=i)B_(r_u), and M_k(E)=E[k]C[k]-E[k+1]C[k-1], for every represented branch i and every integer 1<=k with 2k<=N+2, (h+1)U_i[k]C[k]+(k+1)(h-k+1)M_k(E)>=0, using integer zero extension.
claims.scope: All-m tip-surplus remains open. The m>=100 tail argument is independently supported informally conditional on the accepted full Jensen theorem; the m<100 universal base is not established here. No actual-first-descent restriction is added.
claims.reason: The tail derivation survives direction, basis, denominator, and boundary review, but does not cover m<100. Finite arithmetic checks are corroborative only; no all-m proof or counterexample was established.

claims.statement: If the exact-ratio tip-surplus inequalities hold for a nonempty ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star at each represented tip and every integer 1<=k with 2k<=N+2, then for every such k and every represented tip i and endpoint 0, A_v[k+1]C[k-1]<=A_v[k]C[k], where A_i=G B_(r_i-1)H_i+zL^N, A_0=LQ+zL^N, and C=GQ; all coefficients are integer-zero-extended.
claims.scope: Exact conditional all-profile implication on the full registered lower-half guard. The endpoint proof requires its own main-product LR fact as well as coefficientwise U0>=Ui. No unconditional comparison is claimed.
claims.reason: Positive order-h ULC curvature and common-convolution main-product LR imply M_k(U)>=lambda_k U[k]C[k]. The surplus pays the E minor. The endpoint uses separate (L,G) LR in addition to U0-Ui>=0.

claims.statement: Under the same exact-ratio tip-surplus premise, W=sum_i r_i A_i satisfies W[k+1]C[k-1]<=W[k]C[k] for every integer 1<=k with 2k<=N+2, with the original private-tip multiplicities r_i.
claims.scope: Conditional informal implication with the same C, exact lower-half guard, and unchanged original r_i multiplicities; not an unconditional registered weighted-deck result.
claims.reason: M_k is linear in its first argument and all weights r_i are positive, so individual tip minors sum without changing multiplicities.

claims.statement: At any fixed profile and guarded rank k, the tip-surplus premise for one represented branch i suffices for the endpoint shifted comparison; the premise for each branch separately suffices for its tip comparison, and hence for the original-r_i weighted tip deck.
claims.scope: Conditional rank-by-rank strengthening of the bridge dependency, using U0[k]>=Ui[k], separate endpoint LR, and positive original multiplicities.
claims.reason: Only the endpoint inequality transports one branch's surplus using coefficientwise dominance; each tip conclusion still needs that tip's own surplus.

limitations: The all-m tip-surplus remains open here because the m<100 base is unproved.
The accepted Jensen theorem is a dependency of the reviewed m>=100 analytic tail.
Finite spot checks are not universal proof.
No unconditional individual or weighted shifted comparison, selected MASS/payment, arbitrary-tree993, or Erdős993 conclusion is established.
The convolution minor arguments are informal and receive no Lean award from this review.
